hypothesis: A bounded measured-rail point-to-line correction of lateral/vertical translation and rotation can reduce return discrepancy without changing forward ICP displacement, worsening registration, inventing stationary travel, or losing the existing labelled-recording alarm gate.
criterion: All six complete recordings. Stationary total travel no worse than matched baseline; each of three named return discrepancies strictly lower (endpoint coincidence is NOT ground truth); accepted registration residual/overlap not worse; weak-axis flag not falsely cleared; no loss of baseline hazardous frames on doubleT_obstacle. Continuous comparison numerical tolerance 1e-9, no integer-count tolerance. Any failed criterion rejects promotion.
method_scope: Original constrained rail-point registration experiment, NOT a reproduction of multi-sensor RailLoMer. Nominal gauge is not imposed by correction; upstream rail selection still has its original nominal-gauge candidate prior. Nonrail validation is disjoint from rail fitting but shares the sensor and ICP initialization. Raw KISS map remains untouched; corrected poses only feed detector association.
promotion: disabled unless every acceptance criterion is met; no post-panel threshold tuning
